text.p: More than 200,000 protesters demonstrated against Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic in central Belgrade on Thursday.

The crowd of supporters of the Zajedno (Together) coalition which packed the city's Republic Square was one of the biggest of the past 32 days of rallies to demand that Milosevic restore opposition victories in local elections last month.
Zajedno had earlier called on Belgraders to bring their families to the protest and to celebrate St Nikolas Day, a traditional family occasion in the Serb Orthodox Christian calendar.
Coalition organisers laid on traditional fare of fried fish, cake and wine to help draw in almost 10 percent of the greater Belgrade population.
Independent Radio Index said the Republic Square was full when the tail of the march, with up to 50 people abreast at some points, was still almost a 1.6 km (one mile) away.
The square has been Zajedno's favoured site for rallies ending the daily marches, and observers say it holds about 100,000 people.
One of the Zajedno leaders Zoran Djindjic told the crowd: "What we are celebrating here is not St Nikolas day, but the day we entered democracy."
"Our good will and tolerance are expressions of our strength. We have entered democracy and will never again leave it," he said.

The protest came the day before a mission from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) was due to arrive in the Serbian capital to investigate the allegations of electoral fraud which sparked the marches.

Milosevic invited the OSCE mission, to be led by former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez, to try to resolve the crisis which has developed into the most sustained challenge to his nine-year-old grip on power.
